reason: The upper digestive tract ends beside the colon outline, so their connection is clear.
expectation: They should form one continuous digestive tube.

alternatives.reason: Placing the eye is another clear way to begin.

effect: The small intestine now connects to the colon, completing the digestive-tube goal. The head still needs its eye and ears.
reaction: It is satisfying to see the separate gut sections form one route.
reason: The eye's optic nerve leads toward the brain in the head, so placing it there fits the remaining goal.
expectation: The eye should be placed in the head with its nerve leading toward the brain.

alternatives.reason: The ears also belong in the head and could be placed first.

effect: The eye is in the head and its optic nerve leads to the brain; the ears still need placing.
reaction: The supplied second eye makes the head model feel more complete.
reason: The ears belong in the head, and their established nerves lead toward the brain.
expectation: The ears should fit into the head with their nerve routes toward the brain.

effect: The ears are in place with their hearing and balance nerves connected to the brain, completing the chapter's goals.
reaction: It is satisfying to see the earlier hearing and balance structures kept together in the head.

mostWorthwhile.text: Joining the upper gut to the colon was most worthwhile: it made the digestive tract a continuous route and clarified that absorbed materials cross its lining.

leastWorthwhile.text: Placing the eye and ears was straightforward and a little repetitive, though their positions and nerve routes made sense.

surprise.text: I noticed that the head model supplied a second eye when I placed the first one.

arbitrary.text: None of the actions felt arbitrary; the pictures and goals made the connections clear.

continue.text: I would probably continue to see how the digestive tract and head join the rest of the body, though I hope the next chapter offers more than straightforward placement.
